title: Evaluation of In-Corpus SimCLR Pretraining for Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition Under Recording-Disjoint Splits
content: Label scarcity limits underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) and motivates self-supervised learning on large unlabeled hydrophone archives, yet the benefit is unclear when training and test recordings may not overlap. This controlled pilot evaluates in-corpus SimCLR pretraining on 176,481 unlabeled log-mel clips pooled from the training partitions of Oceanship, QiandaoEar22, and a reconstructed VTUAD corpus. A ResNet-18 encoder is evaluated on each corpus under recording-/clip-disjoint splits with linear probing and full fine-tuning against ImageNet and random initialization. Under linear probing, SimCLR trails ImageNet features on VTUAD (accuracy −0.0829, paired p = 0.017) and QiandaoEar22 (−0.0533, p = 0.012), with only a non-significant edge on Oceanship; after fine-tuning, gaps are small and SimCLR is nominally worse on VTUAD accuracy (−0.0388, p = 0.034). VTUAD probes show a stable validation–test gap and higher training-recording separability than both controls; normalization controls leave this intact. The main analysis covers 45 downstream configurations on one encoder; robustness checks add two encoders, corpus balancing, and checkpoint-rule variants. Extending pretraining to 100–200 epochs does not close the gap, channel-varying augmentation halves it, and a VICReg objective reproduces it (Section 4.4). Across seeds 42/43/44, cross-encoder standard deviation of downstream test accuracy is 0.002–0.009; both probe-accuracy deficits replicate in the same direction on all three encoders (p ≤ 0.017). These observations are consistent with recording-specific information in the learned features, but do not establish that it causes the deficits. We derive design requirements for future UATR evaluation: cross-site pretraining, channel-varying augmentation, balanced corpus sampling, and recording-identity controls.
